mathematical_checkpoints: For every nonempty outer fiber, including a null one, a translated half-copy of its same-parity core partner has mass at least 2^{-d}m>E at the integer midpoint. The midpoint therefore lies in the core.
The transversal property makes the representation p=2w-v unique. Within a target group all core partners are distinct and different from the target; outer and core sources are disjoint.

Failure at all actual mixed points implies the strict ordinary maximal-depth inequality because ordinary maxima are attained. Keeping a minimum-volume core fiber when summing gives max V_w<m+E and D(K_w)<Gamma(1+E/m), with no L-dependent loss.
Every local hypothesis follows from rho<=theta. One ambient tilt generates paired opposite offsets; the local lemma permits all lists, so simultaneous compatibility imposes no missing condition.

The guarantees Gamma V_w+alpha E_w are averaged over candidate points, not over repeated charges to a single cap. Since alpha>Gamma and E>0 their average strictly exceeds the target. E=0 is settled separately by the largest fiber.
Purely integer cuts retain the whole target fiber. General containing halfspaces reduce to parallel through-point halfspaces. Zero-volume fibers contribute no positive charge.

The theorem does not establish the small-tail hypothesis for arbitrary bodies, does not give an explicit numerical rho_d, and does not cover d=1 by this proof. The elementary weak-bound comparison is recorded separately in the review note.
